newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close slightly lower on Wall St bounce.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close slightly lower on Wall St bounce.

text.p: French shares closed just below Wednesday's closing high, maintaining a level not seen since early 1994, as Wall Street bounced back from opening losses on profit-taking.
The Paris market had been in the red all day and the blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 1.56 points or 0.07 percent at 2,211.81 while the futures contract was down eight at 2,211.
Paris hit a closing high and a year high of 2,218.57 on Wednesday on a rally in the wake of the U.S. presidential elections. Its all-time high stands at 2,360.98, reached on February 2, 1994.
* Volume was 4.26 billion francs of which 2.5 billion in CAC-40 shares.

* Dealers noted that there had been some short covering at the end of the day, pulling shares back up, but there was some uneasiness about how long the French shares could stay at the new levels without any fresh impetus. "The good news is now in the prices, we are waiting for a new series (of good news), said Daniel Jamet, analyst at FIMAT.
* Today's drop in U.S. weekly jobless claims was benign to the market but did not change the outlook and was shrugged off in Paris. German unemployment hit a record high in September.

* Aviation related stocks were boosted by the 120 plane order by USAir for Airbus. Zodiac up 0.31 percent, at 1,530 francs, Labinal up 3.81 percent at 872 franc, Intertechnique up 3.29 percent at 816 francs while Latecoere was suspended limit up.
* Labinal also boosted by "buy" recommendation from Cheuvreux de Virieu which also upgraded 1996 and 1997 forecasts.
* Thomson-CSF closed 0.69 percent higher at 161.50, after initial losses. The company announced it would have the majority in an Air Traffic Management joint venture with Siemens AG of Germany.
* Bouygues Offshore, a unit of French construction company Bouygues, said on Thursday in a statement it had priced its 6.8 million global share offering at 127 francs per share.
* Elf down 0.21 percent at 425 francs after a U.K. refining and distribution merger with Chevron and Murco.
* Roussel-Uclaf up 2.03 percent at 1,359 francs on renewed Hoechst buy-out talk.

* Salomon down 1.91 percent in second day of slide following profit warning by Japanese unit Salomon & Taylor Made Co as well as on the back of bankruptcy of a Japanese distributor. Shares have more than doubled in price this year.

* Essilor slips 0.21 percent to 1,427. Communications director Nicole Micheletti told investors' seminar that the net debt of the eye glass and contact lense maker should remain steady at two billion francs at the end of 1996, unchanged from its level at the end of the first half.
* Bertrand Faure, up 5.92 percent at 188.00, said it had 25 percent higher sales in October.
* Bollore Technologies slipped one franc to 558. It said after close that its nine month sales slipped to 16.06 billion francs from 16.44 billion.
* Ciments Francais closed 2.18 percent lower at 164.00 francs before saying its nine month's sales slipped to 9.183 billion francs from 9.584 billion last year.
* Dassault Electronique was the biggest riser on Thursday, up 6.27 percent to 449.00 francs following 5.6 percent higher nine-month sales.
* Industrial pipes maker Nordon was biggest faller with 4.49 percent decline to 340.00 francs.
-- Marcel Michelson, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
